title: Flaming Youth Revue cast and learning to tap dance
summary: He describes the troupers, including Virginia Moore and Frank Kulman, and how he picked up tap steps from other acts and later partner Eddie White.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yeah, but wait a minute, we've skipped too much, here. Just a second.
All right.
-- Cause I'm very interested in that
I danced with a boy -- the boy -- not the girl.
Oh, I see.

She did her own single number, I did xylophone numbers -- one of the boys was a piano player, and he was a singer, great voice, he could dance, he was a multiple talented kid. And, the other boy was very young and his mother travelled with us.
No, kidding?

He and this Virginia Moore and Jackie Sherrick Shererard, there names just came to me, were from Columbus, Ohio. She was very small, and the authorities used to come, thinking she was a young girl, and yet she had a degree from Ohio State University.
For heavens sake, how funny.
She got talking and started using big words to the authorities, they didn't know what to think of her. They thought she was a very precocious little child.
How funny that a girl with a degree --
Yeah Jack -- Jackie Sherrick Shererard has dance studios around Columbus, Ohio, round those places. Frank Kolin Culman was the other guy's name. His father was a -- painted scenery
for the opera.
I'll be darned.

He was very talented, he had an awful sickness and it affected his voice and his body and he died oh, I saw him, I remember when we were at the Blackhawk in '37, and he was very is -- sick at that time.
But --
-- so anyway the act was good --
-- but did you --
-- I was -- in fact Tiboo produced it, you know.
Oh, he did?
Yeah, he --
But did you do any time steps or what kind of dancing did you do?
Yeah, dancing we did -- we did tap-- tap danced.
You tapdanced?
Yeah, sure.
You're kidding?
Sure, I loved it. And then I -- after Frank left --
Well who -- who -- who taught you, did they break you in and teach you the steps and things?
Oh, how do you learn how to dance --
You pick them up?
There was no instructions a century ago (unintelligible).
Yeah, you just fell in with their routines.
Yeah, you'd be on a bill with six or eight other acts and they were dancing and you were watching --
Yeah.

And first thing you know maybe one of the kids in one of their dance act -- have a boy that's dancing, so you're outside the theater or the stage door or something he's doing a time step, he shows you this --
Yeah.
-- or he does another step, show me that. You know, he shows you --
YEAH.
That's the way you learn it --
That's terrific.
First thing you know, you start doing a thing and Frank Kulman, knew some real good routines, so I -- Picked them up from him and we did them together --
Well, that's terrific.

-- then when he got sick and left, we had Eddie White was a dancer who came -- was a better dancer. And he was a dancing nut, that was all he did all day, he just be tackling everyplace. If you walk down the street he's bound to be -- you know, walking -- so we'd wait for trains at the railroad
station, he's say come on, we'd go around the side, you know how they used to have those wooden loading platforms?
Yeah.
He'd start dancing there, see? It was great -- you know, travel in those days was fun. Now It's -- really enhanced theater and everything --
Yeah, sure.
